claims: "focusing on the historical custom of reciting pesukim from Yirmiyahu in the Beit Knesset Farasi and the Mustarabim community in Aram Sova" - the transcript mentions this custom was done in the Beit Knesset Farasi and separately in the Mustarabim community (Beit Knesset HaGadol), but does not state the Mustarabim community was in Aram Sova (Halab is mentioned for Aram Sova, while Mustarabim are discussed as the local inhabitants prior to Sephardim).
summary: Mr. Harari discusses the musical makam used for Parashat Mikess, which is associated with the Bet HaMikdash and the holidays of Pesah, Shabuot, and Sukkot. He also describes a specific tefillah recited when taking out three sefarim, focusing on the historical custom of reciting pesukim from Yirmiyahu in the Beit Knesset Farasi and the Mustarabim community in Aram Sova.
questions: Why is Makam Siega used for Parashat Mikess?
What is the significance of the pesukim from Yirmiyahu when taking out three sefarim?
Which communities practiced the custom of reciting special tefillot during the procession of the sefarim?
How did the customs of the Mustarabim differ from other Kehilot in Halab?
